summary: This Google Cloud documentation page is a code sample titled "Query a Firestore collection with multiple eq filters." It shows how to chain multiple equality (eq) filters on a Firestore collection of cities, using examples in C#, Go, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python and Ruby. The page links to guides on compound queries and querying data in Cloud Firestore; most of the surrounding text is site navigation and boilerplate.
one_line: Google Cloud Firestore code samples in seven languages showing how to chain multiple equality filters in a collection query.
key_facts: The code sample is titled "Query a Firestore collection with multiple eq filters" and is part of Google Cloud's Firestore samples.
The C# sample queries db.Collection("cities") with WhereEqualTo("State", "CA") chained to WhereEqualTo("Name", "San Francisco").
The Go sample builds denverQuery with Where("name", "==", "Denver") chained to Where("state", "==", "CO").
The Go sample caliQuery filters state equal to "CA" and population less than or equal to 1000000.
The Go sample query filters country equal to "USA" and population greater than 5000000.
The Java sample creates chainedQuery1 with whereEqualTo("state", "CO") followed by whereEqualTo("name", "Denver").
The Node.js sample chains where('state', '==', 'CO') with where('name', '==', 'Denver') on citiesRef.
The Node.js sample also filters where('state', '==', 'CA') with where('population', '<', 1000000).
The PHP sample chains ->where('state', '=', 'CA') with ->where('name', '=', 'San Francisco') on $citiesRef.
The Python sample uses FieldFilter("state", "==", "CO") chained with FieldFilter("name", "==", "Denver") to build denver_query.
The Python large_us_cities_query combines FieldFilter("state", "==", "CA") with FieldFilter("population", ">", 1000000).
The Ruby sample chains where("state", "=", "CA") with where("name", "=", "San Francisco") into chained_query.
Each code sample notes that developers must set up Application Default Credentials to authenticate to Firestore.
